title: Snap Apps document extraction — v1 (AU)
description: Strict output contract for receipt/invoice extraction. Used with strict:true tool use or output_config.format. EVERY value is wrapped in a Field object carrying a confidence and, optionally, a bounding box (`bbox`). `bbox` is NOT requested from this vision-extraction path today — no field below is ever emitted with one by `apps/server/src/extraction/provider.ts`, which is `additionalProperties:false`-strict about what it parses. Where a box exists, it comes from a SEPARATE pipeline: on-device grounding (`docs/ON-DEVICE.md` OD-7, `document_field_grounding`) matches an already-extracted value back to a span in the phone's own DocDOM after the fact. `docs/GAPS.md` C1 measured the alternative — asking the model to point at pixels for every field — on 24 receipts and found it bought nothing (zero hallucinations caught either way) while costing accuracy (minimax-m3 fell from 87 correct answers to 69), so it is deliberately not adopted for THIS schema's fields. The model MUST return value:null with a reason rather than guessing — a confident wrong ABN silently creates an unclaimable GST credit, which is worse than a missing one.

doc_type.description: Internal classification. In Australia a supermarket receipt is often ALSO a tax invoice — that is decided by the validators from the ATO elements, not here.

says_tax_invoice.description: ATO element 1: are the words 'tax invoice' printed prominently on the document?

currency.description: BT-5, ISO 4217. Default AUD when absent.

supplier.description: ATO elements 2 and 2a: seller identity and ABN

buyer.description: ATO element 7: required when the sale is $1,000 or more incl GST

rounding_amount.description: BT-114. Australian cash sales round to 5c; record the difference here rather than distorting a total. Written to `documents.rounding_amount`, which already had a NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and an existing (previously dead) posting rule in `transactions.repo.ts` that creates a rounding split whenever this is non-zero.

gst_inclusive_statement.description: ATO element 6 alternative: a statement such as 'Total price includes GST' instead of a separately itemised GST amount.

card_last4.description: Last 4 digits ONLY. Never return a full or partial PAN beyond 4 digits — doing so drags the platform into PCI-DSS scope. Enforced in code, not only by this instruction: `extraction/types.ts#maskCardLast4` truncates to the last 4 digits at parse time (`provider.ts`), again at `run.ts#toDocument` / `repo.ts#saveExtraction`, and `documents.card_last4` is itself `CHAR(4)` — a longer value fails the write rather than being silently accepted (ticket S1, `docs/STATEMENTS.md` §12 Lane S).

unit_code.description: BT-130, UN/ECE Rec 20: EA, LTR, KGM, MTR, HUR, DAY

unit_price.description: BT-146. Up to 6 decimals — fuel is priced at $1.899/L.

gst_category_code.description: BT-151, UNCL5305. S = standard 10%, Z = GST-free (fresh food, most medical, education), E = exempt/input-taxed, O = out of scope.

tax_subtotals.description: Peppol BG-23, one entry per (category, rate). NOT part of what the model is asked to return — `apps/server/src/extraction/provider.ts` never puts this key in the parsed shape. Per-cent GST arithmetic is exactly the kind of thing a vision model is bad at and code is exact at (see the header comment of `extraction/tax-subtotals.ts`), so these are DERIVED deterministically, after extraction, from `lines` and `header.tax_amount`/`header.payable_amount` by `taxSubtotalsFromLines()`, then stored in `document_tax_subtotals`. This property documents that OUTPUT shape — the Peppol wire/export form — not an input the model must supply. An Australian grocery receipt legitimately mixes GST-free fresh food with taxable packaged goods, and a single total cannot express that; that is why the derivation exists, not why the model is asked for it directly.

legible.description: Is this a true and clear reproduction? The ATO only accepts an electronic copy of a receipt if it is. false should send the capture back to the user for a re-shoot rather than into the ledger.

unread_regions.description: Areas of the document that could not be read at all. Being explicit here is more useful than a low confidence score on a guessed value.

BBox.description: [x, y, width, height] normalised 0-1 relative to the page. Powers tap-to-source in the review UI.

null_reason.description: REQUIRED whenever value is null. 'not_present' (the document genuinely lacks it), 'illegible' (it is there but unreadable), 'ambiguous' (several candidates, no basis to choose).

MoneyField.description: Decimal amount in the document currency. Return the number as printed; never round, never convert currency.

value.description: ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Australian documents are overwhelmingly DD/MM/YYYY — resolve ambiguous dates that way, and set confidence below 0.9 when the day/month order cannot be proven from the document itself.

trading_name.description: BT-28 / BT-45. Often the only name on a receipt.

abn.description: 11 digits, no spaces. Transcribe exactly what is printed — do NOT repair a number that fails the checksum, and do not infer one from the business name. The validators run the mod-89 check and an ABR lookup; a fabricated ABN defeats both.

state.description: NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, ACT, NT
